title: AI subscriptions worth paying for — a founder's quick top-ten list
summary: Rapid-fire opinion list of AI-adjacent spend worth it: a better agent search tool, Gemini, Railway for hosting, Tesla, upgrading SaaS tiers for API/MCP access, Claude Fable 5, site analytics and Home Assistant over Google Home/Alexa. Mostly vibes, few specifics.
takeaways: Pay for API/MCP access tiers on tools your agent needs
Home Assistant beats closed smart-home assistants

title: Quantum reservoir computing — nine atoms forecasting weather
summary: USTC researchers in Hefei built a quantum reservoir computer from nine interacting atoms that beat classical baselines on weather prediction. The reservoir needs no training, only the readout is trained, and quantum noise is used as the fading memory that time-series forecasting needs.
takeaways: In reservoir computing only the linear readout is trained
Noise can be a feature when the task needs recent-weighted memory

title: Baidu Unlimited OCR — 3B local model parsing 100-page PDFs in one pass
summary: Baidu's Unlimited OCR is a 3B-parameter, MIT-licensed model that reads whole documents (up to ~100 pages) in a single pass, preserving tables, headings, formulas and reading order. Runs locally, so it can replace a messy preprocessing stack in RAG and document-search pipelines.
takeaways: Whole-document OCR keeps cross-page structure that page chunking loses
Local MIT-licensed model means private docs never leave your machine

title: LLM identity confusion — Claude and Grok claim to be Chinese models
summary: Researchers queried four American LLMs via API without system prompts, in Chinese, about their identity. GPT and Gemini answered correctly, but Claude Opus 4.8 claimed to be Chinese (mostly Qwen) 60% of the time and Grok 97% (mostly DeepSeek), a likely trace of distillation-style synthetic training data.
takeaways: Raw API calls without a system prompt reveal training-data provenance
Training on another model's outputs leaks its self-identity

title: Cochlea — Wi-Fi side-channel attack on Ring cameras
summary: Benn Jordan's Cochlea is a Python tool that runs on a Raspberry Pi with a monitor-mode Wi-Fi adapter and passively fingerprints encrypted traffic from cloud cameras like Ring. It detects when a camera sees motion and when the owner opens live view, logging to CSV, which shows how much activity leaks without breaking encryption.
takeaways: Encrypted IoT traffic still leaks activity through timing and volume
Cloud cameras in the home reveal occupancy patterns to passive sniffers

summary: Comment-bait post for a motion-editing website with a one-word transcript and no named subject.
drop_reason: no subject: comment-bait caption, empty transcript

title: Jacobian conjecture — AI-claimed counterexample explained via maps
summary: Explains the claim that an AI found a counterexample to the century-old Jacobian conjecture: whether a polynomial map with constant nonzero Jacobian determinant is always globally invertible. Walks through Jacobians as area ratios using the Mercator projection.
takeaways: The Jacobian is the local area/volume scaling of a map
Local invertibility from a nonzero Jacobian doesn't automatically mean global invertibility

title: Clipping economy — brands pay per-view for creator content reposts
summary: CNN report on clipping: content-rewards platforms list campaigns from creators, brands and tourism boards, and clippers cut, caption and repost the footage for about $1-1.50 per thousand views. Top operators claim eight-figure revenue and pitch it as a pocket-sized billboard replacing traditional ad buys.
takeaways: Distribution is being outsourced to swarms of paid clippers
Payouts are ~$1-1.50 CPM, so volume is the whole game

title: Agentic OS on Claude Fable 5 — cron loop with earned autonomy
summary: Blueprint: a cron-run loop.sh where a cheap model triages changes, Fable 5 plans as manager, Sonnet executes and a fresh Fable reviews. Tasks earn autonomy after 20 passes at 95% and lose it below 90%, refusals come back as HTTP 200 so scripts must check stop_reason, and a goals directory reruns regression tests daily.
takeaways: Check stop_reason for refusals, not just exit codes
Grant autonomy per task type from logged pass rates
Keep daily regression tests so old builds can't break silently

title: DIY media brand — agent-written features and carousels instead of paid press
summary: Instead of paying for 'as seen on Forbes' features, have an agent DM influencers offering features, rewrite their top posts into articles with a humanizer repo, then turn articles into Instagram carousels with a carousel-generator repo and pitch collabs. Repo names and prompts are comment-gated.
takeaways: Paid press features are a pay-to-play product
Repurpose one strong post into article plus carousel

title: Humanizer skill for Claude Code — strip AI tells from your writing
summary: Build one Claude Code skill from the blader/humanizer repo (based on Wikipedia's 'Signs of AI writing'), plus structural tells from the StoryScope paper and dataset. Wire it into CLAUDE.md rules and hooks so every human-facing doc gets a de-AI pass.
takeaways: Wikipedia's Signs of AI writing is a ready-made style blacklist
Enforce it with CLAUDE.md rules or hooks, not just an optional skill

title: Nvidia closed-loop cooling — why it grows demand for chillers
summary: Nvidia's Rubin closed-loop liquid cooling removes evaporative water use but still needs chillers, heat exchangers, dry coolers and liquid cooling units. Modine (MOD), via its Airedale subsidiary, hit $1.1B data center revenue (+73%) and got $165M upfront from a hyperscaler. Read the engineering, not the headline sell-off.
takeaways: Waterless cooling shifts spend to more cooling hardware, not less
Check order books before reacting to headline-driven sell-offs

title: Elite flight signals — tracking how the ultra-wealthy hedge instability
summary: Three signals: a vibe-coded art project tracking oligarch private-jet departures, a Forbes report on villas, yachts and golden-visa demand, and Douglas Rushkoff's story of billionaires asking how to control security forces after 'the event'. Ends with a pitch for a paid leadership program.
takeaways: Private-jet departure tracking is a crude public signal of elite risk perception

title: Car flipping agent — Facebook Marketplace MCP plus Kelley Blue Book
summary: Connect an AI agent to a Facebook Marketplace MCP tool, have it search your keywords each morning, compare listings against Kelley Blue Book using browser tools, message sellers and text you when something is below market. Split each step into a scheduled skill.
takeaways: Marketplace MCP plus price lookup automates deal sourcing
Break pipelines into small skills and schedule them

title: Blender rigid-body spaceship — motors, constraints and drivers for flight
summary: Ian Hubert shows physics-driven vehicle animation in Blender: active/passive rigid bodies, hinge and spring constraints, motor constraints pushing against the ground as thrusters, gravity off, and custom properties wired via drivers with scripted expressions for throttle and lights. Mentions Erindale's XInputReader addon for gamepad control.
takeaways: A linear motor constrained to an immovable object acts like a thruster
Put thrust over the center of mass or the ship tumbles
Expose custom properties and drive them with scripted expressions for interactive control

title: Scroll World skill — one-shot animated scrolling websites
summary: Scroll World is an open-source agent skill for Claude Fable 5 or GPT-5.6: describe a site, approve generated stills, and it turns them into video clips and stitches a scroll-animated page. The creator's fork adds mobile fixes and budget tiers for Higgsfield spend.
takeaways: Approve stills before spending on video generation
Budget tiers matter because video credits drain fast

title: Time complexity patterns — ten loop shapes to recognize in interviews
summary: Cheat sheet mapping code shapes to Big-O: hash lookup O(1), halving loop O(log n), single and sequential loops O(n) and O(n+m), loop plus binary search and divide-and-conquer O(n log n), nested and triangular loops O(n²), branching recursion exponential, permutations O(n!).
takeaways: Triangular loops are still O(n²)
Recognize the loop shape to read off complexity fast

title: DIY fractional CFO — finance API sync plus AI analysis skills
summary: Sync transactions from a finance API into your own tables, then run agent prompts that categorize income and expenses, flag waste and spot under-investment, refining each into a reusable skill. Pitched as a replacement for a $15k fractional CFO.
takeaways: Own your financial data in tables before handing it to an agent
Turn repeated analysis prompts into skills

title: Liquid AI Antidoom — FTPO training to kill reasoning doom loops
summary: Antidoom is Liquid AI's open-source pipeline that finds the exact token restarting a repetition loop, marks it rejected, picks up to 20 alternatives, and trains with Final Token Preference Optimization (FTPO) plus a KL-like regularizer in logit space so reasoning isn't damaged.
takeaways: Targeting the single loop-restart token fixes repetition surgically
Regularize in logit space to avoid wrecking general reasoning

title: Fable 5 plus GPT-5.6 routing — Codex plugin inside Claude Code
summary: Install Codex and the Codex plugin for Claude Code, then build a /route skill: Fable 5 interviews you and plans, GPT-5.6 executes, Fable reviews and loops until done. Splits usage across two subscriptions.
takeaways: Use the stronger planner as reviewer, the other model as executor
Cross-vendor routing stretches both usage limits

title: Obsidian knowledge vault — viral 'Anthropic engineer brain' graph
summary: Viral claim that an Anthropic engineer's Obsidian vault (~8,900 nodes) is structured like a neural network and runs internal decisions. Unverified hype, but the underlying point is that disciplined markdown linking in Obsidian scales into a real knowledge graph.
takeaways: Claims are unsourced, treat as inspiration only
Consistent linking is what makes a vault useful

title: Nintendo static recompilation — native Zelda and Mario Kart ports
summary: Static recompilation projects turn Switch games into native apps: Tears of the Kingdom on Apple Silicon Mac and iPhone (~90fps on a MacBook Air), Skyward Sword HD on Windows, Linux, Steam Deck and Mac at 60fps/4K with a mod manager, and Mario Kart 8 Deluxe on iPhone/Mac with online play. Bring your own game copy.
takeaways: Recompiling once ahead of time beats emulating at runtime
Community-shared shader lists cut stutter for everyone
